newsitem.title: USA: Bonneville still limiting sales to off-peak hours.
newsitem.headline: Bonneville still limiting sales to off-peak hours.

text.p: The Bonneville Power Administration continued to limit next-day power sale offers to off-peak hours only, though it has lifted volume limits on hours 0200 PDT through 0500 PDT, the agency said Thursday.

The federal power marketing agency's price for hours 0100 to 0600 on Friday was unchanged from Thursday at $13.00 per megawatt hour (MWh). BPA also offered electricity during the hour ending 2400 on Friday at $15.00, they said.
Sales volume during hours ending 0100, 0600 and 2400 PDT were still limited to 600 megawatts, but there were no limits on sales between 0200 and 0500, a Bonneville trader said.
For Northwest buyers only, the Portland, Ore.-based Bonneville was offering power from 0200 to 0500 on Friday at $9.00.
Price offers were the same for Saturday deliveries.
Bonneville attributed its lack of surplus power during heavy-load hours to the normal seasonal decline in hydroelectric power output.
